title: Choose your world — cyberpunk mafia anime
question: Pinned world: cyberpunk mafia anime. These five are hand-crafted for you from our conversation. Take one, or re-roll for a fresh hand.

options.label: The Syndicate Dossier
options.lineage: yakuza record rooms after dark: case folders, hanko seals, red ink, CRT terminals behind venetian blinds
options.thesis: The portfolio as a capo's case files: every shipped product is a sealed file stamped CLOSED-DELIVERED, and the numbers are the family's books.
options.viewport: A lamp-lit record room: the name on a brass plaque as the case cabinet's owner, six case files on the desk each stamped with a shipped product, the CAN DO motto stamped on the cabinet, metrics inked as ledger columns.
options.risk: Needs real stamped-record density, not a paper texture slapped on cards; every stamp must carry a true figure.

options.label: The Wanted Wall
options.lineage: Akira-era bounty boards: photocopied WANTED posters, paper grain, red seals, neon kanji, CCTV static
options.thesis: The portfolio as a back-alley bounty wall: each product is a wanted poster with its bounty in installs, and the engineer is the most-wanted name on the board.
options.viewport: A dark alley wall: the name poster centered under a neon kanji sign, each product below as its own poster with bounty figures (20k+ installs), the CAN DO tagline rubber-stamped across the wall, metrics as bounty totals.
options.risk: The strongest meme of the set; reads cheeky unless the poster craft goes full density with real figures as bounties.

options.label: The Chrome Sleeve
options.lineage: edgerunner cyberdecks: boot sequences, HUD chrome, phosphor readouts, implant loadouts, neural sync
options.thesis: The portfolio as a neural interface booting: products are installed chrome, skills are augmentations, and impact metrics are system telemetry.
options.viewport: A boot sequence: the name as the deck's identity line, CAN DO as the boot message, six products as installed-chrome modules with telemetry bars (installs, cost delta, velocity), metrics as a live system readout.
options.risk: The most obvious cyberpunk lane; must commit to deck grammar (boot, sync, telemetry) and never fall back to neon gradients over rounded cards.

options.label: The Crew Board
options.lineage: Akudama-Drive job boards: mission walls, case photos, red string, blueprint grids, fixer call sheets
options.thesis: The portfolio as a fixer's job board: every shipped product is an executed heist with its status stamp, and the metrics are the crew's payout score.
options.viewport: A mission wall: the name as the crew's call sign across the top, each product pinned as a completed job with its heist ledger (20k+ installs, 35% cost cut), CAN DO as the crew rule, impact stats as the scoreboard.
options.risk: Jobs-to-products maps cleanly, but the metaphor can overpromise; status stamps must stay factual (shipped, not 'score earned').

options.label: The Yakuza Ink
options.lineage: irezumi full-body suits: sumi ink, gold leaf, needle lines, skin-paper, neon glow after dark
options.thesis: The portfolio as a boss's tattoo suite: each product is a panel of ink on the back piece, revealed panel by panel, and the numbers are set in gold leaf.
options.viewport: The back piece: the name as the central medallion, six product panels inked as scenes down the spine, CAN DO inked as the motto band, metrics as gold-leaf engravings beside each panel.
options.risk: The most artful card and the hardest to keep scannable; each ink panel must carry its product's facts inside the artwork, not beside it.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What this category ships, executed impeccably: dark gradient hero, big name, code motif, rounded cards.
canonCard.viewport: The arrangement a visitor expects, at full craft.
